title: Published template manifest
description: The manifest at templates/<template-id>/template.json, written by scripts/publish-template.mjs when an APPROVED revision is published. It is the bundle's machine-readable contract: a consumer generator reads this and nothing else to decide which class to call, which spec provider to use, which data file to copy, where the assets are and which dependencies a build file needs. Nothing downstream may infer any of that from the directory listing or from the README, because a manifest that knows less than the prose is how a generated build file stops compiling. Read it through scripts/lib/template-bundle.mjs#readManifest, which normalises the two dependency-key shapes in the wild and back-fills the consumer contract for bundles published before schemaVersion 1.1.0.

schemaVersion.description: On-disk contract version for this manifest. 1.0.0 is every bundle published before the consumer contract existed: it carries the flat className / specClass / specProviderClass triple and no entrypoint, data or resources block. 1.1.0 adds those, plus version, graphComposeVersion and pageCount. A reader must accept both; a writer emits 1.1.0.

id.description: Template id. This is the directory name under templates/ and the argument every consumer command takes.

displayName.description: Human-facing name, e.g. "Mint Editorial CV". The template id is kebab(displayName) unless --template-id overrode it.

version.description: Bundle version, independent of the harness version and of the GraphCompose version. Preserved across republishes rather than incremented: a bump is an editorial decision about whether consumers must re-integrate, and the publisher cannot make it. Set it explicitly with --version. Absent on 1.0.0 bundles, where readers assume "1.0.0".

docKind.description: Document kind — invoice, cv, proposal, coverletter, report. It names the data file (<docKind>-data.json) and is how a consumer command knows what to copy, so it is required even for a template that ships hard-coded content.

className.description: SIMPLE name of the published template class, e.g. "MintEditorialCvTemplate". src/<className>.java must exist in the bundle. The fully-qualified form is entrypoint.templateClass; this field stays simple because verify-published-template.mjs and the bundle scan both address the file by it.

specClass.description: Fully-qualified spec type the template composes against. It is NOT necessarily a class the bundle ships: invoice-classic names com.demcha.compose.document.templates.data.invoice.InvoiceDocumentSpec, which comes from GraphCompose itself. Null for a template that takes no spec. Duplicated by entrypoint.specClass on 1.1.0 bundles.

specProviderClass.description: Fully-qualified provider that loads the spec from the data file. Passed to the renderer as --spec-provider. Null for a template that takes no spec. Duplicated by entrypoint.providerClass on 1.1.0 bundles.

entrypoint.description: The three fully-qualified names a generated runner needs, so a consumer generator substitutes rather than infers. Absent on 1.0.0 bundles, where readManifest back-fills it from className plus the package declared in src/<className>.java.

templateClass.description: Fully-qualified template class — the one a runner instantiates and calls compose(session, spec) on.

specClass.description: Fully-qualified spec type, same value as the top-level specClass.

providerClass.description: Fully-qualified spec provider, same value as the top-level specProviderClass.

data.description: Where the example data is and what a consumer should rename it to. Null when the template ships hard-coded content and publishes no data file — that is a real shape, not a defect, and a consumer command must not invent a data file for it.

example.description: Path to the example data, relative to the bundle root, e.g. "data/cv-data.example.json".

runtimeName.description: Filename the example is copied to in a consumer project, e.g. "cv-data.json". This is the name the spec provider looks for, so it is not a suggestion.

dataFile.description: DEPRECATED. The pre-1.1.0 half-answer to the same question: it named the example but never the runtime name, so a consumer still had to know the rename convention. Present on invoice-classic. Readers should prefer data.example; writers no longer emit it.

resources.description: Template-owned resources, relative to the bundle root. Null when the bundle ships neither — a template drawing no icons and loading no images has no resources, and a consumer command must not create empty directories for it.

assets.description: Directory holding icons, images and any custom fonts, e.g. "assets". Null when the bundle ships none.

manifest.description: The resolved asset manifest, e.g. "assets-manifest.json". A template reads it rather than hardcoding an icon extension, so it must travel with the assets. Null when the bundle ships no assets.

graphComposeVersion.description: The GraphCompose version this bundle was published against, lifted out of dependencies so a catalog can print it without parsing coordinates. Redundant with the io.github.demchaav:graph-compose entry, and deliberately so: the catalog reads one field, the pom generator reads the map.

pageCount.description: Pages in the published preview render. Counted from preview/output-page-N.png, falling back to 1 when only the older single-page preview/output.png is present. Null when the bundle ships no preview.

sourceProject.description: Project id in the workspace this bundle was published from. Traceability only — a consumer never needs it, and nothing in the bundle may resolve a path through it.

sourceRevision.description: The APPROVED revision this bundle is the published form of. The one place revision vocabulary is allowed to survive into a bundle: it is metadata, not a path, and the portability scan allows it here for exactly that reason.

sourceCommit.description: Harness commit at publish time, or null outside a git checkout. With sourceRevision and graphComposeVersion this is what lets a rendering service log which template produced a document.

publishedAt.description: When the bundle was written, ISO 8601.

fonts.description: Font roles the template needs and how each resolves, taken from the revision's assets-manifest.json. A consumer reads this to know whether anything must be registered by hand: source "graphcompose-bundled" needs the fonts artifact on the classpath and nothing else, while "custom" or "google-fonts" means a file under assets/fonts must be registered. Null when the revision had no asset manifest.

role.description: Where the font is used — heading, body, signature, fallback.

family.description: Family name as the template asks for it, e.g. "Poppins".

fontName.description: GraphCompose FontName constant, e.g. "POPPINS", when the family is one it bundles.

status.description: Whether the role resolved cleanly at publish time.

registration.description: How the font reaches the document — default-fonts, standard14, or a manual registration call.

notes.description: Anything a consumer would otherwise have to discover by rendering.

dependencies.description: What a build file must declare for this bundle to compile and render, read from the source project's render-runner/pom.xml at publish time rather than hardcoded — the manifest used to list graphcompose and jackson while a bundle needing graph-compose-fonts said so only in its README. Two key shapes exist on disk: the current "groupId:artifactId" form and the pre-1.1.0 shorthand ("graphcompose", "jackson"). Readers must accept both; scripts/lib/template-bundle.mjs#normaliseDependencies is the one place that expands them.

additionalProperties.description: Version, or null when the coordinate was declared without one and inherits it from a parent pom.
